sec.t: ff.8.1 What shall we watch tonight?
sec.p: The main form of entertainment is - historically - TV. I found an analysis of the IMDb catalogue showing the types of content offered over the last 70 years.

sec.t: ff.8.2 Squid Game in real life?
sec.p: By the way, I found a guy who recreated it in real life. Oh, and in one day it got 42 million views. More than the Netflix show.
(Smart) TV may well be the most traditional and comfortable way to enjoy content, which increasingly comes from online platforms. But, but, but…

Testifying to the trend towards the smartphone, mobile advertising revenue has recently overtaken TV's, going from 20.8% to 34% share in less than a lustrum. I hadn't used that word in a while (at least five years).

sec.t: ff.8.5 Killing boredom (and not human beings)
sec.p: Where do video games fit into all this?
Enough tech talk. The best way to unwind is still a pint of beer. If you're looking for a bar, here's the map below.
To wrap up this digression on boredom, a thought on the need (or not) to kill time. Reading is also a weapon we have to do it, right?
